name: Terpander
bio: Terpander of Antissa on Lesbos was a musician and poet who, according to ancient tradition, settled at Sparta in the early seventh century BC. He is said to have won the first musical contest at the Spartan festival of the Carneia and to have brought Lesbian song to the Peloponnese.

Tradition credits him with replacing the four-stringed lyre with one of seven strings and with founding the citharodic nome, a solo hymn sung to the lyre. Only a few lines, mostly quoted by later writers, survive under his name, and some of these are of doubtful authorship.

poems.title: Fragment 1
poems.author: Terpander
poems.text:
Zeus, the beginning of all, the leader of all;
Zeus, to thee I bring this gift for a beginning of hymns.

poems.title: Fragment 2
poems.author: Terpander
poems.text: Of the Far-Darting Lord come sing me, O my soul.

poems.title: Fragment 3
poems.author: Terpander
poems.text: Let us pour to the Daughters of Memory and their Lord the Son of Leto.

poems.title: Fragment 4
poems.author: Terpander
poems.text: O [Sons] of Zeus and Leda, saviours most beautiful.

poems.title: Fragment 5
poems.author: Terpander
poems.text: To thee we will play new hymns upon a lyre of seven strings, and will love the four-voiced lay no more.

poems.title: Fragment 6
poems.author: Terpander
poems.text: Where bloom both the spear of the young men and the clear sweet Muse, and eke that aider unto noble deeds, Justice that goeth in broad streets . . .
